scenario.summary: The Interlock ransomware group has introduced a PHP-based Remote Access Trojan (RAT) variant, delivered via the KongTuke campaign using social engineering and malicious PowerShell scripts. The malware establishes a command-and-control channel through Cloudflare Tunnels and fallback IPs, performs extensive host and domain reconnaissance, and maintains persistence via registry run keys to facilitate lateral movement through RDP.

meta.rationale: The hunt should start by targeting all Windows workstations and servers. Prioritize hosts where the 'scoping-weird-php' query returns hits, then pivot to the PowerShell command lines.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is deploying a PHP-based RAT via PowerShell web cradles, executing the PHP interpreter from user-writable AppData paths to evade standard software audits and maintain remote access.

blind_spots.risk: A host running the Interlock PHP RAT without telemetry coverage will remain invisible to this entire hunt workflow.
blind_spots.question: Which hosts are not reporting process or network events?
blind_spots.requires: Complete coverage of hb_process_activity and hb_network_connection
blind_spots.remediation: Audit agent health and ensure universal coverage across the workstation estate.

blind_spots.risk: Attackers can encode the WebClient download or IEX call; simple LIKE matches on process_cmd_line will fail.
blind_spots.question: Was the PowerShell loader obfuscated to bypass command-line keywords?
blind_spots.remediation: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) and ensure it is ingested into hb_script_activity.

hunt.name: Interlock PHP RAT Loader and Deployment
hunt.description: This hunt targets the initial execution and deployment phases of the Interlock PHP RAT variant, as seen in the KongTuke/LandUpdate808 campaign. We look for the characteristic PowerShell 'web cradle' that downloads from Cloudflare tunnels and subsequently executes a portable PHP binary from the user's AppData directory. The hunt pivots between PowerShell process arguments, rare PHP binary locations, and Cloudflare C2 infrastructure to identify infected endpoints where standard detections might have been bypassed.

nodes.label: Scope hosts with non-standard PHP binaries

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, user_name, process_path FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) = 'php.exe' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\php.exe') AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts that have executed or currently host a PHP binary within a user profile, a common marker for this RAT's deployment.
config.expected_signal: Hosts running PHP from a user directory. Benign hits may include developers with local environments (XAMPP/WAMP), which will be baselined in the next step.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%powershell.exe' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%webclient%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%iex%' AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%trycloudflare.com%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%schtasks%/delete%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the specific PowerShell command line used to download and execute the Interlock RAT payload via IEX.
config.expected_signal: PowerShell processes using WebClient to download from a tunnel URL and piping to IEX. This is a high-confidence indicator for the 'KongTuke' delivery mechanism.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) as path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as hosts, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) = 'php.exe' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\php.exe') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 3
config.description: Identify instances of PHP binaries that are unique to a very small number of hosts, filtering out legitimate development tools.
config.expected_signal: A binary path seen on 3 or fewer hosts. PHP is not a standard business application and its presence should be rare and justifiable.

nodes.label: Connections to fallback IPs or tunnel domains

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{fallback_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) LIKE '%.trycloudflare.com') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Capture any network telemetry originating from the host that matches the report's C2 infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: Outbound TCP/UDP activity to the specific IPs or Cloudflare subdomains. While trycloudflare.com is a shared service, its appearance alongside the other indicators is high-weight evidence.
